hazard: Inadequate information transfer on suicide risk

reports.title: Margaret Stringer: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: As per the evidence of , Nightingale's is not a secure unit and a resident with a similar history to that of Ms Stringer would no longer be admitted to the Home. Should there be a concern in relation to a resident who was already admitted at the home, a system of 1:1 care would be implemented which would restrict access to any items. An urgent referral would therefore be arranged for assessment of the resident and the resident would be discharged to a more suitable placement/acute hospital.
promises.summary: Residents with similar histories will not be admitted; 1:1 care will restrict access to items and urgent referral to suitable placement will be made

concerns.quote: Whereas the court heard evidence that Nightingales would not accept another patient with an equivalent medical profile/history and that, should a resident within one of Nightingales' homes require access to items to be restricted, they would be given 1:1 support pending a mental health assessment and discharge to a more appropriate facility, it was not possible for the home concerned to advise the court as to how and by whom the lead in question had been returned to Mrs Stringer. concerns.hazard: access to restricted items by resident without supervision

concerns.quote: The court heard evidence as to the potential detrimental effects of isolation and loneliness in the elderly, including evidence from the court appointed expert that isolation can be very corrosive, that it is the single most potent causative risk factor for depression in the elderly and that it can have a very detrimental effect on a person's mental state. The court heard evidence and/or found that a number of steps had not been taken pertaining to the transfer of information concerning Mrs [name redacted] risk of suicide. They included the following: i. The care coordinator should have requested that the acute hospital make a referral to the Mental Health Liaison Team for a review; ii. It would have been good practice for a further professionals meeting / CPA review to have taken place prior to formal discharge and no later than just after discharge

reports.title: Marlene McCabe: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There remains the potential for a lack of understanding amongst clinicians as to how urgent referrals into the PIMHT should be made.
concerns.hazard: lack of understanding of urgent referral process

concerns.quote: There is inconsistent availability of access to mental health records across the service providers and information sharing between service providers using different data bases is difficult.
concerns.hazard: inconsistent access to mental health records

concerns.quote: There is a residual risk that reference to drug and/or alcohol misuse in mental health referrals and/or assessments may lead to the missing of a mental health diagnosis and that circumstances may arise in which assumptions are made concerning substance misuse.
concerns.hazard: risk of missing mental health diagnosis due to substance misuse assumptions

concerns.quote: There is a residual risk of non-communication of material information pertaining to patients' mental health between healthcare providers.
concerns.hazard: non-communication of material mental health information

concerns.quote: There is a risk that delayed assessment of patients who may appear to be or are reported to be intoxicated will give rise to a loss of opportunity to identify signs of psychosis.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in communicating mental health‑related information between healthcare providers. The earlier report focuses on suicide risk transfer details, while the later report notes a broader residual risk of non‑communication of material mental health information.
